facts.text: The original car was estimated at 621.70 newtons of air resistance; the changed car at 620.18 newtons (0.244% less). Lower resistance is the goal.
The model predicted less air resistance, but the design was not accepted. Fresh reduction or local prediction agreement is insufficient; step refused.
The biggest actual movement was 3.600 mm, using Hood contour. At normal scale, a movement this small is easy to miss. Orange in the Change view marks movement; it is not heat.
The protected part of the car, including the passenger cabin, stayed exactly in place.
Keep the original shape. Inspect the failed checks before trying another bounded body region. A smaller movement is not guaranteed to pass: very small changes can be lost in numerical noise.
This run used a trained prediction model. It has not been checked by an independent physics-based flow simulation or a wind tunnel.

headline: Lower predicted resistance; step not accepted

technicalFacts.text: The predicted change and freshly calculated change differed by 0.024 N. Small test changes predicted -1.49128 N; a separate calculation of the final shape found -1.51520 N. Disagreement is 1.60%: the absolute difference divided by the size of the predicted change, times 100. This compares two model estimates. It is not real-world model accuracy or the percentage improvement in the car.
We have not yet established how reliably the model predicts the effect of these small shape changes. A tiny numerical improvement is not enough to claim a better real car.
The local run took 377.6 seconds including preparation and checks. The original-car calculation took 75.2 seconds. Testing the changed car took 86.0 seconds.
Sensitivity highlights where the model thinks a small shape change could affect air resistance. It is a suggestion to test, not proof that a change will help.
